subject: article_02_multi_case.pdf - Case #2
bodyText: A 61-year-old male patient suffering from plaque psoriasis was administered his first dose of Zolapamine at 75 mg. Three days after the administration, he developed a larger and more painful area of induration, measuring approximately 8 cm, at the abdominal injection site. This local reaction was accompanied by a low-grade fever of 38.1 degrees Celsius that lasted for one day. He was evaluated to rule out possible cellulitis; an ultrasound demonstrated soft-tissue edema without any abscess formation, and blood cultures returned negative results. Due to the adverse event, Zolapamine was held for one cycle and later restarted at a reduced initial dose alongside premedication. Following this management strategy, the patient experienced no recurrence of the symptoms.

classifications.reason: The article describes a specific identifiable patient who experienced a reportable adverse drug reaction (injection-site induration and fever) following administration of Zolapamine.
